No sequence came through with your message — the text of the protein sequence is missing, so there's nothing for me to identify yet.

Please paste it and I'll take a look. A couple of things that will help:

- **The raw sequence** (FASTA or bare one-letter code is fine). If it came from a PDB/mmCIF `SEQRES` block or from `ATOM` records, three-letter codes work too.
- **Any header, chain ID, or filename** that came with it — a PDB ID, UniProt accession, or AlphaFold-style `AF-XXXXXX-F1` name in the file would identify it outright and save guessing.
- **Whether it's one chain or several** concatenated, since a mixed sequence will confuse any motif-based reasoning.

One caveat so you know what to expect: in this session I have no network access and no sequence-search tools — no BLAST, HMMER, or UniProt lookup. So I can't run a homology search for you. What I can do is identify it from my own knowledge of protein sequences and recognizable motifs (characteristic active-site patterns, signature termini, well-known model proteins like lysozyme, GFP, ubiquitin, hemoglobin, etc.), and tell you clearly how confident I am. If the identification needs to be authoritative, the definitive step is a BLASTp against NCBI `nr` or a UniProt search, which you'd need to run where you have connectivity — I'll say so plainly rather than guess if the sequence isn't one I recognize.

## ANSWER

UNABLE: no sequence was included in your message. Paste the sequence (plus any PDB ID, chain, or accession from the file) and I'll identify it from knowledge — note that I have no BLAST/UniProt or network tools in this session, so I cannot run a homology search.
